title: Etale cohomology of one geometric point
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $C=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\bar c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to C$ be a geometric point of $C$ [def-weil-geometric-point] ($\Omega$ any algebraically closed field with a homomorphism $k\to\Omega$, for instance $\bar c=\mathrm{id}_C$). For an abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $C_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] with geometric stalk $F_{\bar c}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], the etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] satisfies $H^q(C,F)=0$ for every $q>0$, and the canonical map $H^0(C,F)\to F_{\bar c}$, the inverse of the isomorphism $F(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(C,F)$ induced by a resolution followed by the germ map $t\mapsto t_{\bar c}$ at the pointed etale neighbourhood $(C,\bar c)$, is an isomorphism of abelian groups, natural in $F$.

proof.text: The spectrum of an algebraically closed field is a strictly henselian local scheme. Transport the algebraically closed structure to its residue field using the residue-field ring equivalence; then the henselian and separably closed residue-field criteria give an instance of IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing. Apply the existing strictlyHenselianSections_geometricStalk_isIso theorem to the given geometric point.

Global sections is exact: identify the global-sections functor with sections at the terminal etale object using Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections. The terminal sections functor preserves epimorphisms on a separably closed field, and its right-adjoint kernel preservation gives the hypotheses of Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels; hence it preserves finite colimits. The derived-functor homology comparison then identifies cohomology of a single sheaf with global sections in degree zero and with zero objects in positive degrees.
